claude.sample_unit: adults recruited from primary care clinics (split into 459 training and 460 test)
models_evaluated: HK Chinese non-laboratory-based pre-DM/DM logistic regression risk model

links.outcome: Calibration of the model after local recalibration/updating using primary care data
links.effect: Recalibrating the regression constant fixed the calibration intercept (original 1.79 to -0.01 in test set; slope 0.69) with AUC unchanged (0.746). More extensive revision or extension added no further calibration gain.
links.quote: Recalibrating the model's regression constant, with no change to the predictors' coefficients, improved the model's accuracy (calibration plot intercept: -0.01, slope: 0.69).

links.outcome: Model calibration when extended to a new population (primary care) with different pre-test probability
links.effect: Original model underestimated risk in the primary care population (intercept 1.79, slope 0.74). Simple recalibration adapted it to the new population. All updated models had AUC-ROC 0.742-0.750 versus 0.746 for the original.
links.quote: The simple recalibration method can adapt the HK Chinese pre-DM/DM model to PC populations with different pre-test probabilities.

links.outcome: Calibration mismatch between development (general population) and local primary care population
links.effect: Original model systematically underestimated absolute pre-DM/DM risk in the primary care population, where prevalence is higher (incidence 53.4%). Original external calibration intercept 1.79, slope 0.74.
links.quote: Calibration plots of the models indicated that the models tended to systematically underestimate the absolute pre-DM/DM risks for individuals in PC.

models_evaluated: Original Hong Kong Chinese non-laboratory-based pre-DM/DM logistic regression risk model

links.effect: Original external validation in PC: intercept 1.79 [1.64, 1.94], calibration slope 0.74 [0.60, 0.87], indicating poor calibration.
links.quote: Poor calibration was indicated by the calibration plot of the original LR model in external validation on the PC population (intercept: 1.79 [1.64, 1.94], calibration slope: 0.74 [0.60, 0.87]).

The calibration plots of the recalibrated models (methods 1 and 2) had an intercept and slope of −0.01 [−0.22, 0.20] and 0.69 [0.51, 0.87], and −0.02 [−0.22, 0.18] and 0.88 [0.65, 1.10], respectively ( Figure 2a and b ).

models_evaluated: Hong Kong Chinese non-laboratory-based pre-DM/DM risk prediction logistic regression model

links.outcome: model calibration and discrimination after recalibration
links.effect: Calibration intercept improved to -0.01 and slope to 0.69 (from baseline intercept 1.79, slope 0.74), while discrimination remained comparable (AUC-ROC 0.742-0.750 vs 0.746).
links.quote: Recalibrating the model's regression constant, with no change to the predictors' coefficients, improved the model's accuracy (calibration plot intercept: -0.01, slope: 0.69).
